points: Pashchur ben Imer, a kohen and false prophet, puts Yirmiyahu in stocks in front of everyone: an early example of cancel culture.
When he's released, Yirmiyahu tells him his name will be "magor misaviv," terror all around, and for the first time names the enemy explicitly: Bavel.
Yirmiyahu is broken by his role and wants to stop speaking, but the message burns inside him like fire.
In the same breath he says "Shiru laShem, halelu es Hashem." We can complain about the hard things and still thank Hashem for the good.
The Malbim on the cursed day of his birth: it was Tisha B'Av, when Menashe killed the prophets. The man who told his father he'd be a navi was later killed by Menashe.
